1.q: וַ⁠יְדַבֵּ֣ר יְהוָ֣ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֣ה בְ⁠מִדְבַּר־סִ֠ינַי בַּ⁠שָּׁנָ֨ה הַ⁠שֵּׁנִ֜ית לְ⁠צֵאתָ֨⁠ם מֵ⁠אֶ֧רֶץ מִצְרַ֛יִם בַּ⁠חֹ֥דֶשׁ הָ⁠רִאשׁ֖וֹן
1.note: The events in this chapter occurred during the same month as the events in Numbers 7. See the note on [7:1](ta:07). That means that these events occurred before the events in Numbers 1–6, which took place during the second month. You could include a footnote to make the timing of this chapter clear to your readers.

If your language would not represent numbers in forms such as **in the second year** and **in the first month**, you could represent these numbers in forms that your language would use. Alternate translation: [in year two … in month one]

The **first** month of the Hebrew calendar includes parts of March and April on Western calendars. You could convert the Hebrew day and month into an approximate date on the calendar that your culture uses. However, the Jews used a lunar calendar, so if you use a solar calendar, the date will be different every year, and the translation will not be entirely accurate. So you may just want to give the number of the day and the name of the month on the Hebrew calendar and say in a footnote approximately what time of year that is on your calendar.
Here, the word **saying** introduces a direct quotation. See how you translated **saying** in [1:1](ta:01).

2.note: Here the word **And** introduces additional instructions that Yahweh is giving to the Israelites. If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [Also, the sons of Israel shall do]

3.note: If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **day 14**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [On the fourteenth day]

Yahweh is using **between the evenings** as a common expression of this culture to mean “when evening begins.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [when evening begins]

These two phrases **according to all its statutes** and **according to all its ordinances** mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [According to all its statutes] or [According to all its ordinances]

4.q: וַ⁠יְדַבֵּ֥ר מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לַ⁠עֲשֹׂ֥ת הַ⁠פָּֽסַח
4.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as a direct quotation. Alternate translation: [And Moses said to the sons of Israel, “Do the Passover”]

5.note: The **first** month of the Hebrew calendar includes March and April on Western calendars. You could convert the Hebrew day and month into an approximate date on the calendar that your culture uses. However, the Jews used a lunar calendar, so if you use a solar calendar, the date will be different every year, and the translation will not be entirely accurate. So you may just want to give the number of the day and the name of the month on the Hebrew calendar and say in a footnote approximately what time of year that is on your calendar. See how you referred to this month in [9:1](ta:09).

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. Here **in the first** refers to the first month, as in verse 1. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [in the first month]
If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **in the first**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [on one]

If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **day 14**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. See how you referred to this day in 9:3. Alternate translation: [on the fourteenth day]
See how you translated this phrase in 9:3. Alternate translation: [when evening began]

6.note: Here the masculine terms **men** and **a man** have a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [people … human]

The author is using **unclean to a person of a man** as a common expression of this culture to mean “unclean because of contact with a dead person’s body.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [unclean because of coming into contact with a corpse]

The word translated as **and** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [and since they were unclean, they were not able]

Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Moses and Aaron. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Moses and before Aaron]

The author assumes that readers will know **that day** refers to the fourteenth day of the first month when the Passover was to be celebrated. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [on the day when the Passover would be celebrated]

7.note: Here the masculine terms **men** and **man** have a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [people … a human]
The pronoun **him** refers to Moses. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [to Moses]
See how you translated this phrase in 9:6. Alternate translation: [unclean because of coming into contact with a corpse]

7.q: לָ֣⁠מָּה נִגָּרַ֗ע לְ⁠בִלְתִּ֨י הַקְרִ֜ב אֶת־קָרְבַּ֤ן יְהוָה֙ בְּ⁠מֹ֣עֲד֔⁠וֹ בְּ⁠ת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
7.note: The men are using the question form to express their strong desire to participate in the Passover celebration. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Yet, we still want to be able to present the offering of Yahweh in its appointed time in the midst of the sons of Israel.]

The men are using the phrase **are we taken away not to present** as a common expression of their culture to mean “are we prevented from presenting” or “are we forbidden to present.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [are we prevented from presenting]

The expression **are we taken away** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [does our uncleanness take us away]

The phrase **present the offering** is a construction in which a verb (**present**) and its object (**offering**) come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [to give the offering]

The people are using the possessive form to describe an **offering** that is for **Yahweh**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the offering for Yahweh]

The people assume that Moses will know that **the offering** refers to the lamb that was killed and eaten during the Passover celebration. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the Passover lamb offering]

8.note: By **Stand**, Moses means to wait where they were while he went to ask Yahweh about their situation. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Stand here as you wait]

By **I shall hear what Yahweh commands**, Moses means he will go to the sacred tent to receive instructions from Yahweh and then report back to tell them. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and I shall go to the sacred tent, find out what Yahweh commands for you, and tell you]

10.q: דַּבֵּ֛ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵ⁠אמֹ֑ר אִ֣ישׁ אִ֣ישׁ כִּי־יִהְיֶֽה־טָמֵ֣א ׀ לָ⁠נֶ֡פֶשׁ אוֹ֩ בְ⁠דֶ֨רֶךְ רְחֹקָ֜הׄ לָ⁠כֶ֗ם א֚וֹ לְ⁠דֹרֹ֣תֵי⁠כֶ֔ם
10.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Speak to the sons of Israel. Say to them that a man, a man, when he is unclean to a person or is on a distant way, for them or for their generations]

Here the masculine terms **a man, a man** and **he** have a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Since the verses that follow use plural forms, you could also use plural forms here. Alternate translation: [A person, a person, when he or she is unclean … then he or she shall do]

In Hebrew, the repetition of **A man, a man** creates emphasis. If your language has different ways to show emphasis, you could use one of those instead. See how you translated this phrase in 5:12. Alternate translation: [Any man]
See how you translated the similar phrase in 9:6. Alternate translation: [unclean because of coming into contact with a corpse]

The phrase **on a distant way** was a common expression meaning “on a long journey” or “traveling far away.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [on a journey far away]

By **for you or for your generations**, Yahweh means that these instructions apply both to the people who were alive at that time and to all their descendants who would live later. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [which applies to you and to your generations]

Yahweh is using a future statement to give an instruction or command. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words **then he will do** using a command or instruction form. Alternate translation: [then he may do]

11.note: The **second month** of the Hebrew calendar includes April and May on Western calendars. You could convert the Hebrew day and month into an approximate date on the calendar that your culture uses. However, the Jews used a lunar calendar, so if you use a solar calendar, the date will be different every year, and the translation will not be entirely accurate. So you may just want to give the number of the day and the name of the month on the Hebrew calendar and say in a footnote approximately what time of year that is on your calendar.
If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **In the second month**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [On month two]
If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **on day 14**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [on the fourteenth day]
See how you translated this phrase in 9:3. Alternate translation: [when evening began]

These **bitter herbs** are a kind of vegetable or plant that has a strong and sour taste. If your readers would not be familiar with what bitter herbs are, you could use a more general term or explain it in a footnote. Alternate translation: [and small plants that taste bitter]
The pronoun **it** refers to the Passover lamb. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [they shall eat the Passover lamb]

12.note: The pronoun **it** in the phrases **from it** and **in it** refers to the Passover lamb. The pronoun **it** in the phrase **they shall do it** refers to the Passover celebration. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [from the Passover lamb … in the Passover lamb … they shall do the Passover]

Yahweh is using a figure of speech here that emphasizes a positive meaning by using a negative word, **not**, together with a mild expression that is the opposite of the intended meaning. If it would be helpful in your language, you could emphasize the positive meaning in a strong way. It is clear in Exodus 12:10 that they must eat all the food or burn any leftovers. Alternate translation: [They shall eat it all or burn any leftovers before morning]

13.q: וְ⁠הָ⁠אִישׁ֩ אֲשֶׁר־ה֨וּא טָה֜וֹר וּ⁠בְ⁠דֶ֣רֶךְ לֹא־הָיָ֗ה וְ⁠חָדַל֙ לַ⁠עֲשׂ֣וֹת הַ⁠פֶּ֔סַח וְ⁠נִכְרְתָ֛ה הַ⁠נֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַ⁠הִ֖וא מֵֽ⁠עַמֶּ֑י⁠הָ כִּ֣י ׀ קָרְבַּ֣ן יְהוָ֗ה לֹ֤א הִקְרִיב֙ בְּ⁠מֹ֣עֲד֔⁠וֹ חֶטְא֥⁠וֹ יִשָּׂ֖א הָ⁠אִ֥ישׁ הַ⁠הֽוּא
13.note: Here the masculine terms **man**, **he**, and **his** have a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [And the person who is clean and is not on a way and ceases to do the Passover, then that person shall be cut off from his or her people, for he or she did not present the offering of Yahweh in its appointed time. That person shall lift up his or her sin]

Yahweh is using **is not on a way** as a common expression of this culture to mean “is not traveling” or “is not on a journey.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase in 9:10. Alternate translation: [is not on a journey]

Here, Yahweh is speaking of separating a person from his community as if that person were **cut off** from his people like a branch being cut from a tree. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. See the chapter introduction for more information. Alternate translation: [then that person shall be expelled from his people]

The expression **shall be cut off from his people** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is the rest of the Israelites. Alternate translation: [then the rest of the Israelites must cut off that person from among them]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb (**present**) and its object (**offering**) come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [he did not give the offering]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe an **offering** that is for **Yahweh**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. See how you translated this phrase in 9:7. Alternate translation: [the offering for Yahweh]

Yahweh assumes that readers will know that **the offering** refers to the Passover lamb that the Israelites were commanded to sacrifice. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. See how you translated this word in 9:7. Alternate translation: [the Passover lamb offering]

Here, Yahweh is speaking of sin as if it were a **burden** that a person could lift up or carry. This speaks of experiencing the consequences of sin. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [That man shall bear his sin] or [That man will be punished for his sin]

14.note: If you decided in 9:10 to translate these verses in such a way that there would not be a quotation within a quotation, you can continue doing that here. Alternate translation: [And if a sojourner sojourns with them … for them]

These two phrases **according to the statute of the Passover** and **according to its ordinance** mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [according to the statute of the Passover] or [according to the ordinance of the Passover]

Here, **statute** and **ordinance** represent laws about the Passover in general, not one specific law. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use expressions that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [according to the statutes of the Passover and according to its ordinances … The same statutes]

The implication is that foreigners must follow all the Passover regulations, but if they do, they can celebrate the Passover. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [he may do the Passover in that way]

Here the masculine term **he** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [so he or she shall do]

The implication is that **you** includes both the **sojourner** and the **native of the land**. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [for you, both for the sojourner and for the native of the land]

Here, **sojourner** and **native** represent sojourners and natives in general, not specific individuals. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use expressions that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and for the sojourners and for the natives of]

Yahweh is using **the native of the land** as a common expression of this culture to mean “people who were born as Israelites.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and for people who were born as Israelites]

15.note: This **day** is the day that Exodus 40:17 refers to, which is the first day of the first month of the second year. So, this event occurred before the Passover described in the first half of this chapter, which took place on the fourteenth day of the first month. If it is helpful in your language, you might want to make it clear that the account that starts in this verse happened before the Passover in [9:1–14](ta:09). Alternate translation: [Now previously, on the day of the raising up of the Dwelling]

The author assumes that readers will know that **the cloud** is the same cloud that led the Israelites when they left Egypt as described in Exodus 13:21–22. You could say this explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the same cloud that went before them when they left Egypt]

The author is using the possessive form to describe a **Dwelling** that was inside the **Tent of the Testimony**. The Dwelling was the inner part of the sacred tent, and the Tent of the Testimony was the outer part that enclosed it. See Exodus 26:1–13 for details, and see how you translated the similar words in 3:25. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the Dwelling that was inside the Tent of the Testimony]

The point of this comparison is that just as **fire** is bright and visible at night, so was the appearance over **the Dwelling**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [it is bright upon the Dwelling, like the appearance of fire]

Here and in 9:16–23, the author uses the present tense to describe things that happened regularly and repeatedly in the past. See the chapter introduction for more information. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a tense that can refer to regular or repeated actions. Alternate translation: [it was]

16.note: The implication is that this situation with the cloud covering the tent in the daytime and appearing as fire at night continued throughout the entire time that the Israelites traveled in the wilderness. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [So it is continually while the Israelites traveled through the wilderness]

By **the appearance of fire is at night**, the author means that the cloud that covered the sacred tent appeared like fire during the night. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. See how you translated the fuller expression of this idea in 9:15. Alternate translation: [and the cloud appeared like fire at night]

17.note: The author is using **to the mouth of the cloud** as a common expression of his culture to mean “when” or “at the time.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And at any time the cloud could be taken up]

The expression **being taken up** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. Alternate translation: [Yahweh taking up the cloud]

It might seem that the expression **where the cloud dwells there** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [And in any place where the cloud dwells]

The author is speaking of the **cloud** as if it were a living thing that could dwell in a place. He means that Yahweh had the cloud stay in a place. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh had the cloud stop and stay]

18.q: עַל־פִּ֣י יְהוָ֗ה יִסְעוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְ⁠עַל־פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה יַחֲנ֑וּ
18.note: It might seem that the expression **upon the mouth of Yahweh** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [Upon the mouth of Yahweh the sons of Israel both set out and camp]

Here, **mouth** represents what Yahweh said or commanded. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [When Yahweh tells them to, … and when Yahweh tells them to,]

The implication is that Yahweh communicated his commands through the movement of the cloud. When it moved or stayed in place, this showed his will for the Israelites’ travel. The phrase **upon the mouth of Yahweh** refers to Yahweh’s commands or instructions. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Upon the mouth of Yahweh, made known by the cloud, … and upon the mouth of Yahweh, made known by the cloud,]

The author is speaking of **the cloud** as if it were a living thing that could live or stay in a place. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar words in 9:17. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has the cloud remain]

19.note: The author is speaking of **the cloud** as if it were a living thing that could decide to stay in one place. He means that Yahweh had the cloud stay in one place. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And when Yahweh has the cloud remain]

The author is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [keep the command of Yahweh]

The author is using the possessive form to describe a **keeping** that is required by **Yahweh**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what Yahweh commanded them to keep]

The word **and** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [and as a result they do not set out]

20.note: The phrase **And it is that** introduces a situation that happened multiple times but not every time. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this with a word or phrase that introduces recurring events, such as “whenever” or “sometimes.” Alternate translation: [And whenever]

The phrase **days of number** was a common expression of this culture to mean “a small number of days” or “a few days.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a small number of days]

20.q: עַל־פִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ יַחֲנ֔וּ וְ⁠עַל־פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה יִסָּֽעוּ
20.note: The expressions **upon the mouth of Yahweh they camp** and **upon the mouth of Yahweh they set out** might seem to contain extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. See how you translated the similar clauses in 9:18. Alternate translation: [upon the mouth of Yahweh they both camp and set out]

Here, **upon the mouth of Yahweh** represents what Yahweh said by using words. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrases in 9:18. Alternate translation: [when Yahweh tells them to, … and when Yahweh tells them to,]

The implication is that when Moses says the Israelites moved **upon the mouth of Yahweh**, Yahweh communicated his will through the movement of the cloud. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. See how you translated the similar phrases in 9:18. Alternate translation: [upon the mouth of Yahweh, made known by the cloud, … and upon the mouth of Yahweh, made known by the cloud,]

21.note: The phrase **And it is that** introduces events that occurred regularly. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use words like “whenever” or “sometimes” to show that these were repeated events. See how you translated this phrase in 9:20. Alternate translation: [And whenever]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [is upon the Dwelling from evening]

The expression **the cloud is taken up** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. See how you translated the similar words in 9:17. Alternate translation: [and Yahweh takes the cloud up … and Yahweh takes the cloud up]

Here, the author could be indicating that: (1) the **cloud** could be **taken up** at any time of the **day** or **night**. Alternate translation: [or the cloud is taken up at any time during the day or night] (2) the **cloud** would sometimes remain over the Dwelling for a **day** and a **night** and then be **taken up**. Alternate translation: [or the cloud is over the Dwelling for a day and a night and then is taken up]

22.note: The phrase **two days or a month or days** presents different lengths of time in order to emphasize that the length of time could vary. The author lists specific time periods as examples and ends with the general term “days” to indicate that these are just examples of possible lengths of time. If it would be clearer in your language, you could make explicit that these are examples and that other lengths of time were also possible. Alternate translation: [Whatever length of time, whether two days or a month or days]

The author is using the expression **days** as a common expression of this culture to mean “a year.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [one year]

The author is speaking of **the cloud** as if it were a living thing that could prolong its stay and dwell in a place. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar clause in 9:19. Alternate translation: [when Yahweh has the cloud remain upon the Dwelling to dwell]

The expression **is taken up** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. See how you translated the similar form in 9:17. Alternate translation: [And when Yahweh takes it up]
